skill.name: role-creator
skill.description: Create and update Codex custom agent TOML files with validated role settings, templates, and installation helpers.
skill.summary: Build standalone Codex custom-agent role files and optional registration entries.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, documentation references, or safely quoted helper-script command substitutions. Confirmed risks are limited to intentional writes under Codex hidden configuration paths and advanced role settings that can enable broad sandbox, network, MCP, or environment-variable access.

remediation.issue: Generated or installed roles can modify hidden Codex configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before writing under ~/.codex and show the exact target path and backup path before changes are made.

remediation.issue: Advanced templates include network, MCP, and environment-variable forwarding settings.
remediation.suggestion: Add stronger warnings near full-role templates and recommend read-only or minimal roles by default.

remediation.issue: MCP server names are interpolated into a generated jq expression.
remediation.suggestion: Validate MCP server names against a conservative character allowlist before adding them to the expression.

content.value_statement: Custom Codex agents require precise TOML files and safe configuration choices. This skill guides users through role inputs, generates agent files, and validates the resulting setup.
actual_capabilities: Collects required role fields before writing custom-agent files.
Creates minimal or advanced Codex agent TOML configurations.
Supports global and project-scoped agent file paths.
Can add optional nickname, sandbox, web search, MCP, and writable-root settings.
Includes shell helpers for writing, installing, and validating role configuration files.
Provides reusable example templates for minimal, restricted, frontend, and full role profiles.
limitations: Requires tomlq and jq for the included shell helper scripts.
Does not verify that referenced MCP servers or external commands are safe.
Can modify Codex configuration files when users run the install script.
Relies on the user to choose safe sandbox, network, and environment-variable settings.

use_cases.description: Define a reusable reviewer role with clear scope, model settings, and developer instructions.

use_cases.title: Standardize project agent setup
use_cases.description: Generate project-scoped agent files so teams use consistent Codex role definitions.

use_cases.title: Prototype advanced agent profiles
use_cases.description: Experiment with sandbox, web search, MCP, and feature settings before committing a role profile.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic agent role
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a project-scoped Codex agent named reviewer. Ask for every required value before writing the TOML file.

prompt_templates.title: Add display nicknames
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Codex agent role with nickname candidates. Validate that the nickname values are unique and use allowed characters.

prompt_templates.title: Build a restricted role
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a read-only Codex agent for research tasks. Keep optional settings minimal and explain what will be written.

prompt_templates.title: Design an advanced MCP-enabled role
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Codex role that uses selected MCP servers and environment variable names. Show the security tradeoffs before writing files.

output_examples.input: Create a reviewer role for this project.
output_examples.output: The skill asks for the role name, description, model, reasoning effort, scope, and developer instructions before creating the agent file.
The skill checks that required keys are present and reports unsupported keys or missing files in clear terms.

output_examples.input: Make a full role with MCP and web search settings.
output_examples.output: The skill can prepare an advanced configuration and warns that network, MCP, and environment-variable settings need careful review.

best_practices: Start with a minimal role and add optional settings only when required.
Review generated sandbox, network, MCP, and environment-variable settings before installation.
Use project-scoped roles when the agent should apply only to one repository.
anti_patterns: Do not create broad danger-full-access roles for routine work.
Do not include environment variable names unless the MCP server truly needs them.
Do not skip confirmation of required fields before writing configuration files.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates standalone Codex custom-agent TOML files and can help register them in Codex configuration.

faq.question: Does it work with project-specific agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents and supports project-scoped agent files under a project Codex directory.

faq.question: Can it configure MCP servers?
faq.answer: Yes, but MCP settings are optional and should be reviewed because they may run external commands or receive environment variables.

faq.question: Does it require command-line tools?
faq.answer: The helper scripts require shell access plus tomlq and jq. The guidance can still be followed manually.

faq.question: Can it modify existing Codex configuration?
faq.answer: Yes. The install helper can update a Codex config file and creates a timestamped backup first.

faq.question: Is the generated role automatically safe?
faq.answer: No. Safety depends on the selected sandbox, network, MCP, and instruction settings.
